title: Structure from motion
description: Nine scenes, each run from the image folder to the reconstruction on an RTX 5060 Ti with the pycolmap incremental mapper (16 CPU threads). AUC@3 is the share of camera pairs…
html:
fastforks sfm turns an image folder into camera poses and a sparse point cloud, the way hloc or COLMAP's feature pipeline do: image retrieval picks the image pairs, a matcher finds corresponding points, a GPU RANSAC verifies them, and the COLMAP mapper (pycolmap) builds the reconstruction.

fastforks sfm scene/images scene/database.db              # COLMAP database: MegaLoc pairs (k=20), LoMa-B matches
colmap mapper --database_path scene/database.db --image_path scene/images --output_path scene/sparse
fastforks sfm scene/images scene/out --reconstruct        # both steps: out/database.db + out/sparse/0
fastforks sfm scene/images scene/out --reconstruct --matcher aliked-lightglue   # the fast matcher (below)

from fastforks.matching import sfm

stats = sfm.colmap_database("scene/images", "scene/database.db", k=30)  # the default matcher, loma-b
print(stats.verified, stats.seconds)  # per stage: retrieval, matching (incl. verification), database
rec = sfm.reconstruct("scene/images", "scene/out", k=30)  # + pycolmap's mapper; rec.model = scene/out/sparse/0
print(rec.registered, rec.points, rec.seconds)

reconstruct and --reconstruct need pycolmap (pip install 'fastforks-core[sfm]'); --mapper global uses GLOMAP's global mapper (pycolmap >= 3.12) instead of the incremental one. --retrieval none matches all pairs, --k sets the pairs per image, --single-camera shares one set of intrinsics among images of the same size, --threshold is the RANSAC inlier threshold (4 px, as COLMAP). The database uses the COLMAP 3 schema; COLMAP 4 and pycolmap 4 read it. Dense matchers (romav2, romav1, loftr) also work (dense_matches most certain pixels per pair, like hloc's match_dense) but take 10x longer and are not in the tables below.

Which matcher

Nine scenes, each run from the image folder to the reconstruction on an RTX 5060 Ti with the pycolmap incremental mapper (16 CPU threads). AUC@3 is the share of camera pairs whose relative pose is within 3 degrees of the reference (100 = perfect), total time = matching front end + mapper incl. model loading, peak memory = GPU memory reserved by the front end. Where a scene was run more than once the range is given in parentheses; differences inside such a range are ties.

Recommendation:

  • loma-b (the default) is the most accurate: better than aliked-lightglue on 8 of 9 scenes (+1 to +3 AUC@3 on Mip-NeRF 360, +15 to +52 on the two wide-baseline ETH3D scenes, where it is the only one with correct poses; its one loss, facade, is 3.6 points) and it registers every image. The cost is about 2x the front-end time (1.5x the total with the mapper), 1.5-1.8x the GPU memory and 2.9 GB of weights.
  • aliked-lightglue (--matcher aliked-lightglue) is the fast alternative: the fastest and smallest front end (1.5-2.3 GB peak, 50 MB of weights), registers every image on 8 of the 9 scenes and reaches 91-96 AUC@3 on the Mip-NeRF 360 scenes. Use it when a minute of time or 1 GB of GPU memory matters more than the last points of pose accuracy, or on scenes without wide baselines.
  • disk-lightglue ties aliked-lightglue overall (better on 6 scenes, worse on 3, by -18 to +2.5). aliked-flexglue ties aliked-lightglue on Mip-NeRF 360 and is the best on facade, but 5x slower; its DINOv3 backbone weights carry Meta's DINOv3 licence terms.
  • These are 6 indoor / garden scenes and 3 outdoor building scenes; other image sets can rank differently. Six of the nine scenes were run once; on the repeated ones the results move by up to 1 (facade) to 5 (delivery area) AUC@3 between runs, so differences of that size on the ETH3D scenes are not meaningful.

The default compute dtype (bfloat16 for loma-b) loses no SfM accuracy: in float32 the poses are the same within the run-to-run range (garden 97.7 vs 97.7, facade 59.0 vs 59.8) at 2x the front-end time.

Every single run and the noise measurements are kept in the maintainers' measurement log (2026-11-13, 2026-11-14).
